text:
anya: quick question — analytics team asked to shorten SIEM export retention from 90d -> 30d for their dev workspace exports. any blockers from compliance/forensics?

carlos: why 30d? are they moving data into another store or just trimming on export side?

anya: they say cost + noise; they'll keep high-fidelity alerts in the primary SIEM for 180d, exports are raw event dumps to a partner S3 bucket that they only need for short replays.

devon: from an infra side we can change export TTL easily, but we need to confirm KMS unwrap lifecycle. current exporter unwraps with a long-lived key grant. if we shorten retention we should use ephemeral unwrap tokens so keys aren't the weak link.

eric-oncall: logging for incident investigations often needs raw traces >30d. who owns the escalation if an incident requires data beyond export TTL?

tamika: compliance note — for regulated investigations we must retain 365d for specified event classes (auth failures, admin actions). is the analytics export filtered? If it omits those classes we might be ok.

anya: it is filtered. exports are: app-logs, user-behavior, anonymized IPs. no admin/audit logs.

carlos: ok that helps. still want to avoid an accidental reduction that removes records we need for a breach. propose: apply 30d TTL only to bucket prefix prod/analytics/dev-exports/* and put a lifecycle policy that moves objects to an encrypted cold archive for 365d if tagged `forensics:true`.

devon: technical note: current lifecycle uses KMS key `km-siem-exports`, which is not allowed to be used by external partners. We wrap/unwrap with a proxy role. If we add an auto-archive step we need the archive key `km-archive` which has different ACLs. that requires an infra change and a short maintenance window.

sec-bot: [policy-check] Found existing IAM role allow: s3:PutObject on analytics bucket by external-partner-acct. KMS decrypt not allowed for external-partner-acct.

anya: so partner can receive exports but can't decrypt unless we unwrap first. that's intended. Proposal: change flow to -> export to partner-encrypted-with-our-key (30d) + copy to internal-archive-key (365d) for objects tagged with `forensics:true`. Partner never gets archive copies.

eric-oncall: sounds reasonable. For incident response we need a documented handoff for when we need archive data. Could be an emergency ticket that triggers a key unwrap and copy to a forensics bucket. Who approves that ticket?

tamika: approval should be sec-eng lead + legal for cross-border requests. Add a short checklist: justification, incident ID, retention window requested, expected recipients.

carlos: operationally: I can implement prefix-level lifecycle + Lambda that tags objects for archive when a filter matches, but that lambda will need kms:Decrypt on `km-siem-exports` and kms:Encrypt on `km-archive`. We'll have to add a constrained IAM role for it.

devon: alternate: use S3 replication with replication-time control and different destination key. replication supports replication time and identity-based encryption. less custom code.

anya: replication seems cleaner. caveat: replication across accounts has eventual consistency delays. forensics folks ok with slight delay?

eric-oncall: 5-10 min delay is fine. critical requests can still request a targeted export snapshot from the primary SIEM.

tamika: also confirm that any replication destination is in-region for data residency rules. cross-region replication requires extra approvals.

carlos: next steps I propose: 1) create RFC for prefix-level 30d TTL + replication-to-internal-archive(365d, km-archive) 2) add IAM role for replication with least privilege 3) update runbook for emergency unwrap and access request 4) narrow scope so admin/audit logs are excluded.

anya: +1. can someone file the RFC and a Jira for the runbook?

devon: I'll file RFC and an infra change PR. assigning to @carlos for IAM + @tamika for compliance signoff.

eric-oncall: I'll update the incident playbook with the emergency archive request flow and add who to ping.

sec-bot: [ticket-created] RFC-5487 created: "analytics export retention scope and archive replication" — link: https://rdrw.atlassian.com/browse/RFC-5487

anya: thanks. one more ask — can we switch exporter unwrap to short-lived tokens (1h) by next week? that reduces key exposure.

carlos: technically doable but requires rolling exporter credentials and updating partner integration docs. we'll do a canary in staging first.

devon: agree. plan: staging canary -> prod small subset -> full rollout. I'll add steps to the RFC.

tamika: reminder: update the data retention policy doc and notify privacy/legal about the scope change.

anya: perfect. thanks everyone. :thumbsup: 

carlos: action items I have: PR for IAM role, add replication config, canary plan. will post ETA in thread tomorrow.

devon: I'll link the PR and the lambda fallback if replication hits a constraint.

eric-oncall: noted — I'll draft the emergency access ticket template tonight and attach to the RFC.

anya: closing loop — if no objections by EOD tomorrow we proceed with RFC and staging canary.
